When the narrative breaks: The trade dies if any of these materialize: (1) a surprise demand destruction signal — Chinese PMI collapse or a sharp US employment miss — that reframes the move as "oil spiked into a recession" rather than "oil signals inflation"; (2) a strategic petroleum reserve release or OPEC+ production surprise that breaks the supply-constraint thesis; (3) the Fed hikes this week but signals it's a one-and-done, causing yields to reverse sharply — oil would lose its inflation-momentum bid; (4) WTI fails to hold $100 on any pullback, triggering momentum-follower stops and revealing the crowded nature of the trade.

The narrative is reassuringly simple: "the market sells the rumor and buys the news." Barron's running "5% yields aren't a death sentence" and Morningstar urging "don't panic" reinforce this buy-the-dip reflex.

The risk is that this isn't a normal hike cycle — oil at $106 with yields at 5.00% and VIX rising 10.2% suggests this may be the beginning of a tightening sequence, not a one-off event, and the historical analogs these articles cite may not apply to a stagflationary backdrop.
